name: Eskimo-Aleut Languages (Genus Template)

formality.description: Eskimo-Aleut languages express formality through kinship-based address and discourse style rather than pronominal T-V distinctions. Respectful language for elders and ceremonial contexts uses specific discourse markers and vocabulary.

gender.inclusiveGuidance: Eskimo-Aleut languages have no grammatical gender. Pronouns do not distinguish gender.

linguisticChallenges.polysynthesis: Eskimo-Aleut languages are extremely polysynthetic — a single word can encode what would be an entire sentence in English. Verbs carry subject, object, tense, aspect, mood, and multiple derivational morphemes. Word-level MT is fundamentally inadequate.
linguisticChallenges.ergativity: Most Eskimo-Aleut languages are ergative-absolutive in case alignment, meaning the subject of a transitive verb and the subject of an intransitive verb receive different case markings. This is the opposite of English/European patterns.
linguisticChallenges.incorporatedMorphology: Noun incorporation is productive — nouns can be incorporated into verb stems to create complex predicates. This creates 'words' that have no single-word equivalent in target languages.
linguisticChallenges.dialectalVariation: Significant dialectal variation across communities, even within the same language. Written standardization is often contested or incomplete.

contactInfluences.notes: Colonial and administrative dominance. English-only schooling policies severely impacted intergenerational transmission.
French administrative influence in northern Quebec (Nunavik) and some Labrador communities.

notes: Genus template for Eskimo-Aleut languages (Inuktitut, Inuinnaqtun, Kalaallisut, Yupik varieties, etc.). All share extreme polysynthesis, ergative alignment, and noun incorporation.
